chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman, so he looked at her head and at a part of her body. Can he marry her daughter? He said: No. When he has seen from her what is prohibited to others, so it is not for him to marry her daughter.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his wife's daughter if he has already viewed her private parts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition for the prohibition of marrying a daughter-in-law based on the father-in-law's prior viewing of her 'awrah' (private parts), distinguishing it from mere marriage. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical act of viewing as the trigger for this specific kinship barrier, rather than the marital contract itself. This ruling is crucial for understanding the nuances of 'mahram' relationships in Islamic family law.
